talk_track: I'm Barry Hess - I spent sixteen years running engineering at a small defense firm and fielded a patented tactical app platform with operators in theater, then watched it die force-wide because nobody built the advocacy chain above the operator. Your live DevSecOps posting says the hire will be 'an early member of a growing team' with 'significant influence on our security architecture,' and lists 'Active Secret or TS/SCI clearance, or the ability to obtain one' as a preference rather than a requirement. Read next to a $9.5M Joint Antenna Marketplace prototype awarded through a competitive SpEC OTA, that posting means the security architecture which has to survive government accreditation is still being drawn while the period of performance burns. The months it takes to get a first cleared owner through adjudication come out of the transition window, not in addition to it - that arithmetic, months-to-field against funded months remaining, is what decides whether a prototype becomes a program. I hold a current TS/SCI, so that clock doesn't start over for me. Worth sketching the accreditation path before the prototype period closes?
